la:noun:dies.html:
dĭes (dīes, ), ēi (ēī, ; et saep.;
dissyl.: di-ei,; also gen. dies, die, and dii—dies, as in acies, facies, pernicies, etc., Enn. ap. ; Ann. v. 401 Vahl.; ap. Gell. l. l.: die, P.; even in , where Gellius reads dies, v. Wagner ad loc., nearly all MSS. have die; cf. Rib. and Forbig. ad loc.; so, die,; ; ; ; ; ; cf. Oud. ad B. G. 2, 23, 1. Die appears to be certain in ; . Also in , Gellius reads dies, where our MSS., except the Cod. Lamb., have diei; perh. those words do not belong to Cicero himself. Form dii,, Rib. and Forbig. after Serv. and Gell. l. l.— Dat., diēī, saep. die, , acc. to ; ; ; ; once dii,, Prol. 13; cf. Roby, Gram. 1, 121 sq.); m. (in sing. sometimes f., esp. in the signif. no. I. B. 1.) [root Sanscr. dī, gleam: dinas, day; Gr. δῖος, heavenly; cf. Lat. Jovis (Diovis), Diana, deus, dīvus, etc. Old form, dius (for divus); cf.: nudius, diu, etc. The word also appears in composition in many particles, as pridem, hodie, diu, etc., v. Corss. Auspr. 2, 855 sq.], a day (cf.: tempus, tempestas, aetas, aevum, spatium, intervallum).
Lit.
In gen., the civil day of twenty-four hours.
Masc.: dies primus est veris in Aquario ... dies tertius ... dies civiles nostros, etc.,; cf. ; ; : REBVS IVRE IVDICATIS TRIGINTA DIES IVSTI SVNTO, XII. Tab. ap. ; and 15, 13 fin.; for which; per dies continuos XXX., etc.,: multa dies in bello conficit unus, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 297 ed. Vahl.); cf.: non uno absolvam die,: hic dies,: hic ille est dies,: ante hunc diem,: illo die impransus fui,; cf.: eo die,; ; fin.; 4, 11, 4; 5, 15 fin. et saep.: postero die,; 3, 6, 3 et saep.; ; ; et saep.: in posterum diem,; et saep.: diem scito esse nullum, quo die non dicam pro reo,: domi sedet totos dies,: paucos dies ibi morati,: dies continuos XXX. sub bruma esse noctem,: hosce aliquot dies,; cf. et saep.: festo die si quid prodegeris,; so, festus,; ; et saep.—
Fem. (freq. in poetry metri gratiā; rare in prose), postrema, Enn. ap. : omnia ademit Una dies,; cf. ; and 998: homines, qui ex media nocte ad proximam mediam noctem in his horis XXIV. nati sunt, una die nati dicuntur, Varr. ap. (uno die, ): quibus effectis armatisque diebus XXX., a qua die materia caesa est,: Varronem profiteri, se altera die ad colloquium venturum, (for which, shortly before: quo cum esset postero die ventum); cf.: postera die, (for which, in the same author, more freq.: postero die): pulchra,: suprema,: atra,: tarda, et saep.—(But ; , read altero, tertio.)—
Connections: postridie ejus diei, a favorite expression of Caesar,: 1, 47, 2; 1, 48, 2 et saep., v. postridie; and cf.: post diem tertium ejus diei,; Sulpic. ap. ; : diem ex die exspectabam,from day to day,fin.; cf.: diem ex die ducere,; for which also: diem de die prospectans, ; and: diem de die differre, : LIBRAS FARRIS ENDO DIES DATO, for every day, day by day, daily, XII. Tab. ap. ; cf.: affatim est hominum, in dies qui singulas escas edunt,; so, in dies,every day,; ; ; ; ; Drak.; 34, 11 al.; less freq. in sing.: nihil usquam sui videt: in diem rapto vivit,; cf.: mutabilibus in diem causis (opp. natura perpetua), (in another signif. v.the foll., no. II. A. 3); and: cui licet in diem ( = singulis diebus, daily) dixisse Vixi, etc., . And still more rarely: ad diem, Treb. Gallien. 17; : ante diem, v. ante.—Die = quotidie or in diem,daily,; : quos mille die victor sub Tartara misi,: paucissimos die composuisse versus,: saepius die,: die crastini, noni, pristini, quinti, for die crastino, nono, etc., v. h. vv. crastinus, nonus, etc.; and cf. ; .—
In partic.
A set day, appointed time, term in the widest sense of the word (for appearing before court, in the army, making a payment, etc.).
Masc.: MORBVS SONTICVS ... STATVS DIES CVM HOSTE ... QVID HORVM FVIT VNVM IVDICI ARBITROVE REOVE DIES DIFFISVS ESTO, XII. Tab. ap. ; Müll.; for which: STATVS CONDICTVSVE DIES CVM HOSTE, acc. to Cincius ap. ; and with comic reference to the words of this law, (found also in ); and freq.: status dies,; ; et saep.: hic nuptiis dictus est dies,; cf.: dies colloquio dictus est ex eo die quintus,; so, dictus,: iis certum diem conveniendi dicit,: die certo,; cf. constituto,fin.: decretus colloquio,: praestitutus,: praefinitus,; : ascriptus, et saep.: quoniam advesperascit, dabis diem nobis aliquem, ut contra ista dicamus,; ; ; ; et saep.: dies ater,an unlucky day,.—
Fem. (so commonly in this sense in class. prose, but only in sing., v. Mützell ad ): ut quasi dies si dicta sit,; so, dicta,; cf.: edicta ad conveniendum,: praestituta,; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; cf. constituta,; ; : certa eius rei constituta, : pacta et constituta,: statuta,: stata,: certa,; ; et saep.: annua,; ; cf. longa,: die caecā emere, oculatā vendere,i. e. to buy on credit and sell for cash,, v. caecus, no. II. B.: haec dies summa hodie est, mea amica sitne libera, an, etc.,: puto fore istam etiam a praecone diem,: ubi ea dies venit (preceded by tempore ejus rei constituto),: praeterita die, qua suorum auxilia exspectaverant,; cf. : esse in lege, quam ad diem proscriptiones fiant, et saep.—
Both genders together: diem dicunt, qua die ad ripam Rhodani omnes conveniant: is dies erat a. d. V. Kal. Apr., etc.,; ; ; —
Hence: dicere diem alicui, to impeach, lay an accusation against: diem mihi, credo, dixerat,: Domitium Silano diem dixisse scimus,.—
A natural day, a day, as opp. to night: ut vel, quia est aliquid, aliud non sit, ut Dies est, nox non est; vel, quia est aliquid, et aliud sit: Sol est super terram, dies est, : pro di immortales, quis hic illuxit dies, ap. : credibile non est, quantum scribam die, quin etiam noctibus,in the daytime,: negat ullum esse cibum tam gravem, quin is die et nocte concoquatur,in a single day and night,; cf. in this signif.: die ac nocte,: nocte et die,; and simply die,; ; cf. also: currus rogat ille paternos, Inque diem alipedum jus et moderamen equorum,; and, connected with nox: (Themistocles) diem noctemque procul ab insula in salo navem tenuit in ancoris,; cf. ; —But more freq.: diem noctemque, like our day and night, i. q. without ceasing, uninterruptedly; ; fin.; ; for which less freq.: diem et noctem,; diem ac noctem, and 45: noctemque diemque,; cf. : continuate nocte ac die itinere,; ; and in plur.: dies noctesque,; ; ; et saep.; also, reversing the order: noctesque diesque, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 338 ed. Vahl.); : noctesque et dies,; : noctes atque dies,; ; ; : noctes diesque,: noctes ac dies,: noctes et dies,; ; and 39; ; cf. also: neque noctem neque diem intermittit,: Galli dies ... sic observant, ut noctem dies subsequatur, Herz ad loc. So, too, in gen.: qui nocte dieque frequentat Limina,: cum die,at break of day,: orto die ( = orta luce),; ; : ante diem ( = ante lucem),: dies fit, late Lat. for lucescit,: de die, in open day, broad day; v. de.—
Dies alicujus (like the Heb. ; v. Gesen. Lex. s. h. v.).
I. q. dies natalis, a birthday: diem meum scis esse III. Non. Jan. Aderis igitur,; cf. in full: natali die tuo, al. So the anniversary day of the foundation of a city is, dies natalis urbis, .—
I. q. dies mortis, dying-day: quandocumque fatalis et meus dies veniet statuarque tumulo, Called, also: supremus dies. ; ; cf.: supremus vitae dies,; . Hence: diem suum obire,to die,; and in the same sense: obire diem supremum,; ; : exigere diem supremum,: explere supremum diem,; 3, 76; and simply: obire diem,; ; ; ; cf. also: fungi diem,.—
I. q. dies febris, fever-day: etsi Non. Mart.,

die tuo, ut opinor, exspectabam epistolam a te longiorem, ;

Transf.
In gen. (from no. I. A.).
A day, for that which is done in it (cf. the Hebr. , the Gr. ἐλεύθερον ἦμαρ, etc.): is dies honestissimus nobis fuerat in senatu,: non tam dirus ille dies Sullanus C. Mario,: equites Romanos daturos illius diei poenas,: hic dies et Romanis refecit animos et Persea perculit, Drak.; cf. ; Ruhnk.; 2, 86; ; Duker.: imponite quinquaginta annis magnum diem,: quid pulchrius hac consuetudine excutiendi totum diem? ... totum diem mecum scrutor, facta ac dicta mea remetior, etc., Sen. de Ira, 3, 36: dies Alliensis, i. q. pugna Alliensis,; : Cannensis, And so even of one's state of mind on any particular day: qualem diem Tiberius induisset,what humor, temper,. —
A day's journey: hanc regionem, dierum plus triginta in longitudinem, decem inter duo maria in latitudinem patentem,; —
In gen. (like , ἡμέρα, and our day, for) time, space of time, period: diem tempusque forsitan ipsum leniturum iras,; so with tempus,; : amorem intercapedine ipse lenivit dies, Turp. ap. ; so in the masc. gender: longus,; ; but also longa,; ; cf. perexigua,a brief respite,: nulla,: ex ea die ad hanc diem quae fecisti, in judicium voco,: ut infringatur hominum improbitas ipsa die, quae debilitat cogitationes, etc.,; cf. fin.; : indutiae inde, non pax facta; quarum et dies exierat, et ante diem rebellaverant,i. e. the term of the truce,; ; fin. (for which: quia tempus indutiarum cum Veienti populo exierat, ).—Prov.: dies adimit aegritudinem,: dies festus, festival-time, festival:—diem festum Dianae per triduum agi, et saep.: die lanam et agnos vendat,at the right time,: praesens quod fuerat malum, in diem abiit,to a future time,; so in diem, opp. statim, Q. Cic. Pet. cons. 12, 48; and simply in diem,; ; .—Esp. freq. in diem vivere, to live on from day to day, regardless of the future, ; ; et saep; cf. the equivoque with de die, under de.—
In partic. (acc. to no. I. B. 2—poet., and in postAug. prose).
Light of day, daylight: contraque diem radiosque micantes Obliquantem oculos,; ; : multis mensibus non cernitur dies,; ; ; also of the eyesight, ; and trop. of the conscience: saeva dies animi scelerumque in pectore Dirae,.—
For caelum, the sky, the heavens: sub quocumque die, quocumque est sidere mundi,; : incendere diem nubes oriente remotae,; ; .—Hence, like caelum,
The weather: totumque per annum Durat aprica dies,: tranquillus,: mitis,: pestilens,.—
The air: nigrique volumina fumi Infecere diem,: cupio flatu violare diem,.
Dies personified.
I. q. Sol, opp. Luna, ; coupled with Mensis and Annus,.—
As fem., the daughter of Chaos, and mother of Heaven and Earth, Hyg. Fab. praef.; of the first Venus, .
